clue.text: Save shellfish when temperature is lowered

indicators.note: lowering the temperature turns hot into cold, so the abbreviation for one swaps for the other

parts.note: C for cold replaces H for hot

explanation.surface: A thrifty cook keeps the prawns once the fridge is turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: Hot (H) becomes cold (C): the H of the shellfish is swapped for C.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrimp is to economise, cutting spending in order to put money by.

clue.text: Extremely wonderful editor provides temporary place to stay

explanation.surface: A grateful guest praises the editor who put them up for a few nights.
explanation.definitionFit: A sofa bed converts into a bed for a guest staying a night or two, a makeshift berth.

clue.text: Regularly break into an Indian side

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every second letter is taken

parts.note: second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: Someone habitually barges into an Indian team's cricket side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Side' suggests a sports team, but here it is a side dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Raita is a yoghurt condiment served alongside curries as an accompaniment.

clue.text: Ship might sink following drills

indicators.note: a drill bores into something, so this letter goes inside

parts.note: abbreviation used in references, as in p. 3f

explanation.surface: A vessel could go under after a session of exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Might sink' reads as a phrase, then F bores into the middle of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mayflower was the vessel that carried the Pilgrim Fathers to America in 1620.

clue.text: Perhaps runner beside winding road could be animal killer

indicators.note: something winding twists and turns, so these letters lose their straight order

parts.note: a runner is a long narrow rug, an example of a mat

explanation.surface: A jogger on a twisty lane is apparently a danger to wildlife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete, but here it is a floor covering.
explanation.definitionFit: A matador is the bullfighter who delivers the fatal sword thrust to the bull.

clue.text: Businessman runs away from electronic puzzle, upset

indicators.note: turned upside down, in a down clue this reads the result from bottom to top
the cricketing abbreviation for runs leaves the word, taken out

parts.note: a Chinese dissection puzzle of seven shapes

explanation.surface: A tycoon flees from a frustrating computer game in a temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnate is a wealthy, powerful figure in industry or commerce.

clue.text: Speed must empower nurses

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the phrase cradles the letters within it

explanation.surface: A slogan says pace of change has to give nurses more power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nurses' looks like the object of empower, but it is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempo is the rate or pace at which something moves, especially music.

clue.text: Days later, supply energetic particles

indicators.note: read as the adverb 'supplely', bending these letters into new shapes

explanation.surface: A delivery arrives a few days late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like a verb but is the adverb from supple, meaning flexibly.
explanation.definitionFit: Delta rays are fast electrons knocked from atoms by ionising radiation, so high-energy particles.

clue.text: Pretty soprano replaces tenor? That's more imprudent

indicators.note: one letter takes the place of another in the word

explanation.surface: A singer asks whether swapping the tenor for a lovely soprano is reckless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty' is the adverb, not the adjective it seems to be.
explanation.definitionFit: Rash means acting hastily without thought, so rasher is the comparative of imprudent.

clue.text: Reportedly trade mushrooms for guns

indicators.note: as it is said, so the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: trade as in purchase, and ceps are porcini mushrooms

explanation.surface: Word has it that someone swaps fungi for firearms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guns' is slang for upper-arm muscles, not weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Guns is gym slang for well-developed upper-arm muscles.

clue.text: Oberon has right to replace Puck at last, but gets fungal growth

indicators.note: one letter is put in the place of another, swapping it out

parts.note: Oberon is king of the fairies in A Midsummer Night's Dream

indicators.note: finally, so only the closing letter of the name is meant

parts.note: final letter of the sprite's name

explanation.surface: In Shakespeare's fairy world, Oberon's servant is supplanted and something mushrooms instead.
explanation.walkthrough: The K at the end of FAIRY KING (the last letter of Puck) gives way to R.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairy ring is a circle of mushrooms or darker grass caused by a fungus spreading outwards.

clue.text: Eccles briefly disorientated in Greek island

indicators.note: cut short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: the setter refers to themself by pseudonym

explanation.surface: The setter admits to getting turned around for a while on holiday in the Aegean.
explanation.walkthrough: Eccles is this puzzle's setter, so the name stands for ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Melos (Milos) is an island in the Cyclades, where the Venus de Milo was found.

clue.text: Cry about Republican fight

indicators.note: one word goes around another, surrounding it

explanation.surface: Someone protests loudly about a Republican scrap in politics.
explanation.definitionFit: A brawl is a rough, noisy scuffle, a disorderly kind of fight.

clue.text: Fancy tea parties outside Bostonian industry end in trouble

indicators.note: read as 'parts', splitting and reworking the letters in a new order
the rearranged letters sit on either side of another word, enclosing it

parts.note: the three letters rearranged and split
work, in American spelling as used in Boston

indicators.note: only the final letter of the following word is wanted

explanation.surface: Elaborate Boston tea parties end up surrounding industrial trouble, a nod to the 1773 protest.
explanation.walkthrough: The Boston Tea Party hint is a red herring; 'Bostonian' simply asks for the American spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: As adjectives, fancy and elaborate both describe something ornate and intricately detailed.

clue.text: Rejects James, perhaps, after overturning snowmobile?

indicators.note: turned over, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Sid James, the British comic actor of the Carry On films

indicators.note: something mobile moves about, so the preceding letters are shifted round

parts.note: the first four letters rearranged, the rest of the word being the signal

explanation.surface: Someone called James is cast off by his family after he flips a snowmobile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snowmobile' must be split into a word and its anagram signal. Sid James was a star of Britain's Carry On comedy films.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown someone is to refuse any longer to acknowledge them, so it rejects them.

clue.text: Lead phased out, which receives attention

indicators.note: put out of shape, the preceding letters are rearranged
to receive is to take in, so one piece is placed inside another

explanation.surface: Lead piping being phased out gets the attention it deserves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like the metal, but it is the verb to lead.
explanation.definitionFit: To spearhead a campaign is to lead it from the front.

clue.text: When visiting Camino de Santiago, the pilgrim returns as prophet

parts.note: Spanish for 'the', as on a Spanish pilgrim route

indicators.note: going back the way it came, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: one who has made the pilgrimage to Mecca

explanation.surface: A pilgrim on the Way of St James turns back, now seen as a prophet.
explanation.walkthrough: The Camino de Santiago is in Spain, so 'the' is put into Spanish. A haji (hajji) is a Muslim who has made the hajj.
explanation.definitionFit: Elijah is the Old Testament prophet carried to heaven in a chariot of fire.

clue.text: Join in with objective, reversing committee's conclusion

indicators.note: going backwards, so the word is read in the other direction
a conclusion is the end, so only the last letter counts

explanation.surface: Someone takes part with a goal, overturning a committee's verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Join in' reads as one phrase; only 'Join' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To integrate is to combine parts into a whole, or to become part of a group.

clue.text: Dress bishop with new mitre

indicators.note: a new version of the word, its letters remade in another order

explanation.surface: Robing a bishop by giving him a fresh mitre.
explanation.definitionFit: Betrim is an archaic verb meaning to adorn or deck out, a synonym of dress.

clue.text: Henry Sopel, for example, included in publication for game

indicators.note: these letters are taken inside another word

parts.note: Jon Sopel, BBC journalist and presenter

explanation.surface: A journalist named Henry Sopel appears in a magazine's games column.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no Henry Sopel: Henry is the unit H and Jon Sopel is the BBC's former North America editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahjong is a Chinese tile game for four players.

clue.text: Animal welfare group appeal for assistance is old hat

parts.note: People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals

explanation.surface: A charity's plea for help is dismissed as old hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old hat' looks like the phrase for something stale, but it is literal: an ancient hat.
explanation.definitionFit: The petasos was a broad-brimmed hat worn in ancient Greece, famously by Hermes.

clue.text: Pureed nut boxed by a customer

indicators.note: pureed food is mashed up, so the letters are mixed
put in a box, so surrounded by another word

explanation.surface: A shopper buys a box of nut puree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' means per, as in prices quoted 'a head'.
explanation.definitionFit: Punter is British informal for a customer or client, or for a gambler.

clue.text: Group of defenders bother stuck up celebrity

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from the bottom

explanation.surface: The back four are annoyed at a big-headed star player.
explanation.walkthrough: MOD is the UK Ministry of Defence; 'stuck up' looks like snobbish but is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Stardom is the state of being famous, the condition of celebrity.

clue.text: One who longs to eat crab's head or claw

indicators.note: eating takes something inside
the head is the top, so only the first letter is wanted

explanation.surface: A hungry diner craves the head or claw of a crab.
explanation.definitionFit: A pincer is the grasping front claw of a crab or lobster.

clue.text: Former Prime Minister: "I am rubbish at Chinese"

parts.note: the majority ethnic group of China

explanation.surface: A former leader confesses that he is hopeless at speaking Chinese.
explanation.definitionFit: Imran Khan, the cricketer turned politician, was Prime Minister of Pakistan from 2018 to 2022.

clue.text: Single friend wanting love in foreign land

indicators.note: lacking, so a letter is left out

explanation.surface: A lone companion short of romance abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepal is a Himalayan country between India and China, a land abroad.

clue.text: Hang out with American in part of West Africa

indicators.note: put out of place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Spending time with a US friend somewhere in West Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hang out' reads as one phrasal verb but splits into fodder and signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghana is a country on the Gulf of Guinea coast of West Africa.

clue.text: Nothing inserted in bottom moved upwards

indicators.note: something inserted is slipped into a gap, so it ends up enclosed by the other word

explanation.surface: Getting stuck with nothing up the backside makes someone jump up.
explanation.walkthrough: Arse is British slang for the buttocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Arose is the past tense of arise, to get up or ascend.

clue.text: Man claiming European is inferior

indicators.note: to claim is to take hold of, so one word holds another inside

explanation.surface: A bigot asserts that someone from Europe is a lesser person.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheap goods are shoddy and low quality, so of an inferior kind.

clue.text: Trick Chicago airport's pilot officer about cloak

indicators.note: turned about, so the whole string reads backwards

parts.note: to swindle, as in 'do someone out of money'

explanation.surface: A con involving an officer at a Chicago airport and some cloak-and-dagger business.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera hood is a hooded evening cloak once worn by women to the theatre.

clue.text: Gerald Ford's introduction aroused warning signal

indicators.note: stirred up, so the letters are thrown into disorder
an introduction is the opening, so only the first letter counts

explanation.surface: A US president's opening remarks stirred up alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: Only Ford is cut down to its first letter; Gerald is used in full.
explanation.definitionFit: A red flag is a sign of danger, flown at ranges and beaches as a warning.

clue.text: Marxist leaders in Ethiopia ensured Mengistu free from blame

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their front letters

explanation.surface: Communist heads in Ethiopia made sure the dictator Mengistu was exonerated.
explanation.walkthrough: Mengistu Haile Mariam led Ethiopia's Marxist Derg regime.
explanation.definitionFit: To redeem someone is to clear them, restoring their good name after a fault.
